clue.text: Element identified by sharp-witted cook at sea

parts.note: quick means mentally sharp, fast on the uptake
Long John Silver is the ship's cook in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A clever ship's cook somehow identifies a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver, the one-legged pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island, sails as the ship's cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the old name for mercury, a metallic chemical element liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Introductions to quiet old men in Iranian city

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their opening letters, so take the first of each following word

explanation.surface: Quiet old men are introduced somewhere in a city in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Qom is a holy city in Iran, a centre of Shia scholarship south of Tehran.

clue.text: Popular monarch snatching time in Bury?

indicators.note: the pair grabs hold of the letter for time and keeps it within them

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A well-liked king or queen grabs time in Bury, the Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the English town; the question mark warns it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to put a body in a grave, which is what burying means.

clue.text: King beheaded mischief-maker in citadel

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: losing its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical mischief

explanation.surface: A king executes a troublemaker inside his fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: A gremlin is the imp blamed for things going wrong with machines; 'beheaded' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex at the heart of Moscow, a citadel in the literal sense.

clue.text: Lacking will, belonging to trial rowing team, one hears

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: in, as in a member in a group, belonging to it; a test is a trial; an eight is a racing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone without a will is, apparently, part of a trial rowing crew.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TEST EIGHT, said aloud, sounds like the legal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a valid will to dispose of one's estate.

clue.text: Symbol of love, in Heaven usually

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Love's symbol is usually found up in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles heaVEN USually.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman goddess of love, and her figure or planet stands as an emblem of it.

clue.text: Relaxing French art treasures originally pinched by gang

indicators.note: pinched by means held tight inside the gang

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang
'thou art' in French is 'tu es', so art is ES

indicators.note: originally means the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: French art treasures are stolen by a gang, who then put their feet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the old verb form, as in 'thou art'; in French that is 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resting and relaxing both mean taking a break from activity to recover.

clue.text: Swindles of husband initially appalling son

parts.note: H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A husband's frauds appal his son.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone is slang for cheating or fooling them, as in 'you've been had'.

clue.text: Material provided by hacks principally, or a shire, oddly

indicators.note: principally means the leading letter of the word
arranged oddly means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Horses, hacks and shires, supply a material, curiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts one to take odd letters, but it rearranges OR A SHIRE into ORSEHAIR after H. Hacks and shires are both kinds of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsehair is a stiff fabric or stuffing made from mane and tail hair, used in upholstery.

clue.text: Pass plant, being extravagant purchaser

parts.note: to spend time is to pass it
thrift is a pink-flowered coastal plant, sea pink

explanation.surface: A shopper splashes out passing over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: THRIFT the plant ironically sits in a word for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift is someone who wastes money recklessly, a lavish and careless buyer.

clue.text: Woman in Missouri shelter mostly the worse for wear

indicators.note: the woman is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
Thea is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman camping in Missouri finds her tent rather tatty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelter mostly' is a tent missing its final letter, and the woman sits between the state and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten describes something shabby and worn out, literally holed by moths.

clue.text: Fling involving pair in 27, for example

indicators.note: involving means containing the other piece

parts.note: 27 across is ELY, a cathedral city and so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A couple have a wild time in Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is one, so 27 stands for SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of unrestrained fun or spending, which is what a fling is.

clue.text: Sings rhythm and blues primarily in part of UK

indicators.note: the letters go inside the country

parts.note: Wales is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone sings rhythm and blues in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to sing with trills, as birds do.

clue.text: Preacher touring north finally rejected beer and cheese

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the preacher surrounds the letter

parts.note: John Wesley was the founder of Methodism, a famous preacher
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A preacher on a northern tour turns down beer and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a Yorkshire valley giving its name to a crumbly white cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Wensleydale is a variety of English cheese, made in that Yorkshire dale.

clue.text: Collieries about to terminate regular pay

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: pits are coal mines, collieries
to end is to terminate

explanation.surface: Coal mines are about to stop paying wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' reverses PITS to STIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary or allowance paid at intervals, as to clergy.

clue.text: Fabric bringing US city half of capital

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: half of means the first three of its six letters

parts.note: London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: New York brings a fabric to half of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Nylon's name is sometimes said to come from NY and LONdon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer woven into cloth, so it is a textile.

clue.text: Like speech praising old archbishop, a right-winger

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A speech praising a former archbishop who was a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud is a historical archbishop, executed in 1645; LAUD also means praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory describes words that express praise, such as a eulogy or commendation.

clue.text: Sign a rough tap damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone signs off a roughly broken tap.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's signature, a sign in the sense of a written name.

clue.text: Islander cheers Welsh girl entertaining crew

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest within, so the girl surrounds the crew

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Thanks to a Welsh girl who hosts a ship's crew from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' and 'ta' are both British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tasmanian comes from Tasmania, the island state south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: The French strip — she washes and irons

parts.note: la is the French feminine 'the'
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A French woman strips off while doing the washing and ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash and press clothes and linen.

clue.text: Study can ultimately define calcified tissue

parts.note: a den is a private study
a tin is a can

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Studying can ultimately define the hard tissue of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentine is the hard calcified layer beneath tooth enamel.

clue.text: Fellow soldier fencing run for dog

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the others surround it

parts.note: co- means joint or fellow, as in co-worker
GI is an American soldier
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A comrade in arms fences off a run for his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests swordplay or a dog run; here it encloses R.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh herding breed, famously the Queen's favourite.

clue.text: Appreciative comment of one first seeing this moulding?

definitions.text: Appreciative comment of one first seeing this moulding?

parts.words: Appreciative comment of one first seeing this moulding?
parts.note: the whole clue imagines the exclamation an admirer blurts on first sight, a two-word British cry of delight that, run together, names the moulding

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the two-word remark 'Cor, nice!'; cor is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an ornamental moulding running round the top of a wall or building.

clue.text: Yankee moneymaker, one with aspirations

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an earner makes money

explanation.surface: An American money-spinner with ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearner longs for something, so has hopes and ambitions.

clue.text: Bill plugging Royal Opera House? Something fishy here

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap within the other piece

parts.note: ROH is the abbreviation for London's Royal Opera House
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bill advertising the Royal Opera House looks suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' also suggests advertising; 'fishy' looks like suspicion but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family, so literally fishy.

clue.text: Bearing left for Luton, possibly

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A compass bearing to the left for Luton.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a town north of London with a major airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton is an example of an airport, one of London's commercial airfields.

clue.text: Woman — old, as it happens

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A woman who is old, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' reads as 'incidentally', but means broadcast in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Garlic mayonnaise made by girl about ten

indicators.note: about means around, so the girl surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Ali is a girl's name
IO looks like 10, ten written in figures

explanation.surface: A girl about ten whips up some garlic mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is 10 written with letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal sauce of garlic emulsified with oil and egg.

clue.text: Foolishness, a crime in country Capone abandoned

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

indicators.note: abandoned means left out of the country's name

parts.note: Italy is a country
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A crime in a country Al Capone left behind seems foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes AL from ITALY, leaving ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Asininity is the quality of being asinine, like a donkey, so silly and stupid.

clue.text: Legendary mountain-dweller, one not appearing up till now

indicators.note: not appearing means the letter goes missing

parts.note: the yeti is the mythical Himalayan snowman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The legendary yeti has not appeared to anyone yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and up till now both mean so far, until the present time.

clue.text: English youth leader seen around large city

indicators.note: seen around means placed around the other letter
leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: L is the clothes-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An English youth leader is spotted around a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely has city status in England thanks to its cathedral.

clue.text: Improved quality of cane men then distributed

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: The quality of canes improved once the men handed them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An enhancement is an improvement that raises something's quality or value.
